text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Monday.

LONDON - Uncertainty about the course of UK monetary and fiscal policy, a further appreciation in the value of sterling and a weak start on Wall Street conspired to drive leading British shares lower for the sixth straight session. The FTSE 100 closed at 4,575.8, down 18.1 points, or 0.39 percent.

FRANKFURT - Shares ended bourse trade lower, hurt by profit taking after the DAX index on Friday surged to a new all-time high on buying tied to the expiry of DAX futures and options and stock options. The DAX-30 index closed at 3,754.72, down 33.55 points, or 0.89 percent. In later screen-based trade the IBIS DAX index ended at 3,748.79, down 39.75 points, or 1.05 percent.

PARIS - Defying Wall Street's downturn, French shares finished slightly higher in a session dominated by technical trade on the last day of the monthly settlement. The CAC-40 index closed at 2,762.20, up 5.10 points, or 0.18 percent.
ZURICH - Shares shook off early weakness to close at a record high in both SMI and SPI indices for the fourth day in a row. The Swiss market index closed at 5,587.8, up 26.0 points, or 0.47 percent.

MILAN - Stocks closed sharply higher to set new closing records, ignoring weak performances on other stock markets and pushing up from early lows on a return of the wave of general euphoria seen last week. The All Share Mibtel index closed at 13,317, up 132 points, or 1.00 percent.

AMSTERDAM - Shares closed slightly lower after a mixed session. The AEX share index touched an intra-day high, but the gain did not hold. The AEX index closed at 860.86, down 1.34 points, or 0.16 percent.

TOKYO - Stocks closed a subdued session mixed, with little effect from the G7 summit in Denver at the weekend, which yielded no surprising news. The 225-share Nikkei average closed at 20,436.14, up 50.60 points, or 0.25 percent.

HONG KONG - Stocks closed weaker after a volatile day which saw the Hang Seng Index hitting a new record high, before retreating on profit-taking and nervousness over China-related red chips, brokers said. The Hang Seng index closed at 15,021.23, down 133.13 points, or 0.88 percent.

SYDNEY - The share market ended a lacklustre session slightly weaker after a fall in the price of gold put pressure on the resources sector. The All Ordinaries index closed at 2,706.3, down 6.3 points, or 0.23 percent.

JOHANNESBURG - Shares finished well up after a weak start and dealers said strength in industrials was mainly due to manipulation by futures traders after that index was at a 100-point premium to fair value. The All-share index closed at 7,286.3, up 52.2 points, or 0.72 percent. The All Gold index closed at 1,015.1, down 12.3 points, or 0.67 percent, while the Industrial index closed at 8,568.8, up 57.3 points, or 1.20 percent.
